fields.h1: Build a Petition Form That Counts Each Signer Once
fields.hero_description: Build a petition form that confirms each signer by email and saves every name to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does With Every Signature
fields.features_subheading: What Emergent builds into a petition, and what stays yours when the campaign closes.
fields.feature_1:
The request and fields drafted for you

Describe the request and who decides it. Emergent drafts the petition statement, addressed to that person, with the signer fields below. Edit any line with a follow-up prompt.
fields.feature_2:
One signer, one signature, by your rule

Choose what counts as one signer: an email, a street address, or a student ID. A second signature that matches one already counted is held for your review, not added to the total.
fields.feature_3:
Alerts at the milestones you pick

Get a Slack or email alert when the petition passes a number you set, such as 250 names, plus a morning summary listing who signed overnight and the streets they live on.
fields.feature_4:
A live count toward your goal

Set the goal the receiving office asks for, or your own. The page shows the count as people sign, and the dashboard splits it by street or by any other field the form collects.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on signatures

Emergent puts no cap on form responses, so a petition that spreads past its first neighborhood keeps taking names. Each signature is a row in a database you own, with its date.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Publish the petition on your own domain, included with Emergent and paid in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it after the campaign.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Petitions and Where Their Signatures Go
fields.tab_content_1:
One name per household, five short of the goal

Neighbors on Alder Street are asking the city for a marked crosswalk at 9th Avenue. The form counts one signature per household, by street address, toward a goal of 84 of the 120 households in the petition area. So far 79 have signed. A second signature from 412 Alder Street is held as a duplicate for the organizer.
fields.tab_content_2:
Emailed links confirm each signature before it counts

Patrons of the Eastgate branch ask the library board to keep it open on Sundays. Each signer gets an email link, and a signature joins the count only after the click, which keeps typed-in fake addresses out of the total. The board sees 1,240 confirmed names, each with a comment, while 87 wait for the click.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each late withdrawal goes up to the dean

A student who misses the withdrawal deadline files a petition with the registrar: the course, the reason, and a note from the instructor. Tomas Reyes asked to withdraw from CHEM 210 on Oct 6, and his advisor approved it on Oct 8. The petition now waits with the dean's office, and the decision goes to Tomas by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
272 signatures, 58 of them from paper sheets

Volunteers at Juniper Park collect signatures at the tennis courts, asking the parks board to add lights. Their scanned paper sheets are read into rows with AI, and 3 names read with low confidence go to a volunteer to check. With 214 signed online and 58 from paper, the petition reaches the board with 272.

fields.howto_title: How to Plan a Petition Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a petition form that reaches the person who decides with a count they can check, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Ask who decides and what counts
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tell signers who sees their names
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the person or office that can grant the request, then ask what they accept. The City of Phoenix speed hump program, for one, wants support from at least 70 percent of residents in the affected area and rejects petitions older than 6 months.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide who counts as a signer before anyone signs: residents of the petition area, library card holders, enrolled students, or anyone at all. Write that rule at the top of the form, and add the field that proves it, such as a street address.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for what the decision-maker will check and what you need to follow up: a name, an address or zip code, and an email. Put an optional comment box last, and leave everything else off the page.
fields.howto_step_4_des: State on the form who receives the list and whether names will be shown publicly. Put updates by email behind their own unchecked box. Signing the petition should never add anyone to a mailing list by default.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a goal and a closing date
fields.howto_step_5_des: Turn the receiving office's rule into a plain number of signatures and show it on the page next to the live count. Pick a closing date inside any age limit the office sets, with a week to spare for delivery.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign with your own email and address, then sign again from the same address with a second email. Under a one-per-household rule, the first counts and the second waits for review. Both rows should land in the table with the date and time.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Hand over the count with the list
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the decision-maker the total and the signer list, sorted the way they will check it, such as by street. Bring a printed copy if the office takes paper, and keep the table for the follow-up.

faq_plan.a: A petition form is the document that carries a petition: a request addressed to an official, with room for the people who back it to sign. The top states what is asked and of whom. Below it, each signer adds a name and the details the recipient will check, such as a street address.

faq_plan.q: How to make a petition form?
faq_plan.ref: How to make a petition form?

prov.original: How to make a petition form?

faq_plan.a: Settle what you are asking for and who can grant it, then build the form. With Emergent's AI form builder, you describe those choices in a prompt, and Emergent builds the page and the signature table, with a live count on top. Change any field later with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: How can I create a free petition form?
faq_plan.ref: How can I create a free petition form?

prov.original: How can I create a free petition form?

faq_plan.a: Build it on Emergent's free tier, which covers building and publishing. Write the request and the signer fields the way you would brief a volunteer, and that description is the whole prompt. Before you share the form, ask the receiving office whether it supplies its own sheet, and match its columns if it does.

faq_plan.q: What should a petition form template include?
faq_plan.a: A petition form template should open with a headline naming the request and the person or body asked to act. Two or three sentences on why come next, then the signer table. Signers back a request; they do not swear to facts. If the office wants a written statement made under oath, ask whether it needs an affidavit form instead.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to sign an online petition form?
faq_plan.a: Share one link where the people affected already talk, such as a building group chat or a neighborhood newsletter. Put a QR code on paper flyers at the place in question, and keep the form short enough to finish on a phone. Emergent sets no cap on form responses: the online petition form stays open however far the link travels.

faq_plan.q: How should a paper petition form be laid out?
faq_plan.hint: How to create an online petition form?
faq_plan.a: Lay it out as a short letter on top of a numbered table. The letter names the request and who it is addressed to. The table has columns for printed name, address, signature, and date, with 20 rows per page. Keep a petition form PDF of that layout so every volunteer prints the same sheet, and number each page.

faq_plan.q: Who should see the names collected on a petition form?
faq_plan.hint: Where is the iu online kelley petition form?
faq_plan.a: Only the people who need them: the organizer, any volunteer checking entries, and the person who decides the request. Keep the full list off any public page; a public count is enough. If volunteers handle signer details, have each one sign your nda form before they get access, and remove that access when the campaign closes.

faq_plan.q: Can a petition form check that signers live in the petition area?
faq_plan.a: Yes, against a list you supply. Emergent builds the form from your prompt. The app can compare each street address or zip code with the streets in the petition area and hold any entry outside it for your review. It checks what the signer typed, not where they live. Tell the receiving office how the list was checked.

faq_plan.q: How do I phrase the request on a petition form?
faq_plan.a: Write the request as one sentence with a verb and a place, such as adding a marked crosswalk at Alder Street and 9th Avenue. Address it to the person or body that can act, and give two or three reasons you can back up. Ask for one change per page, and split a list of demands into separate petition forms.

faq_plan.q: What signer details should a petition form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out anything the decision-maker will not check, such as birth dates or phone numbers. A name and an email cover a petition, plus the one detail that shows a signer qualifies. A full profile of each person belongs on a personal information form, which is a different job from showing support for one request.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Venngage, Formstack, Jotform, PandaDoc, WordLayouts), one petition platform, one advocacy how-to and a county's own petition form. They hand over a blank sheet. This page shows what a working petition form does after people sign: it counts one signature per household toward the threshold the receiving office sets, holds a signature until the signer confirms their email, routes a student's academic petition to the dean, and merges scanned paper sheets with online signatures. It tells the reader to check the receiving office's own rules first, with the City of Phoenix speed hump program as the sourced example. Every example is local and civic; no party, candidate or contested issue.
